description: Out of 18 IPOs reviewed, 11 are currently trading above their original issue price. 7 IPOs are currently trading below their issue price.

faq.a: An SME IPO (Small and Medium Enterprises Initial Public Offering) is for smaller companies looking to raise capital. They list on separate platforms like NSE Emerge or BSE SME, with different rules compared to mainboard IPOs.
The 'issue price' is the fixed price per share at which the company offers its shares to investors during the IPO.
The 'current price' is the latest available market price of the share on the stock exchange, reflecting what buyers and sellers are willing to trade it for now.

faq.q: How do I apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility or through your brokerage firm's online platform. Your money remains blocked in your account until shares are allotted.
'Allotment' is the process where shares are distributed to successful applicants after an IPO closes. If demand is high, shares might be allotted on a pro-rata basis or through a lottery system.
